incidents.vector: Exploited vulnerabilities in Microsoft software to infiltrate a government email server, using a toolkit configured to collect correspondence with NATO and EU institutions.
incidents.impact: Romanian intelligence (SRI) detected and contained the intrusion, attributing it to the Russian FSB-linked group Turla; no evidence found that sensitive information was stolen.

incidents.vector: Supply-chain compromise — a reseller named CryptoBillis distributed wallets implanted with hidden spy chips between August and September 2026.
incidents.impact: Trezor shipped a firmware update to brick the backdoored devices and cut 80% of its supplier network; the same supplier was also linked to spy devices found in Ledger wallets.

incidents.vector: Compromise of Maileva's online mail and parcel delivery platform.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 22 million users was stolen, most of them corporate employees who received paychecks, invoices, and business mail through the service.

incidents.vector: Attackers obtained employee data from a third-party cloud service provider used by TSMC; the company says its own network was not compromised.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 46,000 TSMC employees was leaked on an underground hacking forum after attackers attempted to extort $200,000 in Bitcoin.

incidents.vector: Compromise of the Spanish reservation platform Amadeus, affecting numerous airline customers.
incidents.impact: Passenger data exposed as part of a broader hack of the Amadeus reservation system impacting multiple airlines.

incidents.vector: Breach of the city's email service provider.
incidents.impact: Personal data of approximately 1 million Osaka citizens was stolen.

incidents.vector: Exploited a flaw in the platform's user accounting system to withdraw funds attackers were not entitled to.
incidents.impact: $2.23 million in crypto assets stolen; the platform's withdrawal rate limit blocked an additional $3 million from leaving before it could be triggered.

incidents.victim: 200+ organizations across 14 countries — government ministries, telecom, defense, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, nuclear, and financial sectors
incidents.vector: Used the open-source ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework to automate credential scanning and password-spraying at machine speed, beginning Oct. 17, 2026 (tracked by CrowdStrike as VAPOR PANDA).
incidents.impact: CrowdStrike confirmed post-compromise activity at nine organizations plus additional credential-scanning and password-spraying activity against at least 12 more; related ARTEX activity separately compromised ConnectWise application credentials and targeted Microsoft 365 tenants and Southeast Asian financial firms.

incidents.vector: Theft of tokens across 11 different cryptocurrencies in what researchers call the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.
incidents.impact: $6.3 billion stolen; Binance froze about $2.8 billion of the stolen stablecoins, leaving roughly $3.25 billion unrecoverable, mostly in Bitcoin and Ethereum. The FBI attributed the hack to the North Korean group TraderTraitor.

incidents.victim: 19 organizations — semiconductor/advanced-manufacturing supply chain, US defense and defense-policy sector, and civil-society/human-rights groups
incidents.vector: Used the open-source Cairn AI penetration-testing framework, paired with Chinese LLMs Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek, to autonomously plan and execute 25 intrusion operations between August and September 2026 (tracked as CL-STA-1238).
incidents.impact: Achieved unauthorized access or data retrieval at 10 of the 19 targeted organizations, exposing more than 1 million personal records at one victim, retrieving military and government identities, creating persistent admin accounts, and modifying a live industry standards-ballot document.

incidents.vector: Abused a vulnerable third-party ScreenConnect extension (RMM+) whose authentication key defaulted to blank, allowing a caller to bypass MFA and push rogue remote-access clients to managed endpoints.
incidents.impact: Installed attacker-controlled ScreenConnect clients on at least 288 computers across 48 organizations within about 90 minutes; ConnectWise disabled the extension across roughly 400 partner environments.

incidents.victim: Government ministries of foreign affairs, defense, interior, and law enforcement agencies in one Middle Eastern and four Southeast Asian countries
incidents.vector: Planted malicious JavaScript directly on government webmail portals and web applications to run an in-browser command-and-control framework (Falcon, aka XG), sideloading malicious Chrome extensions.
incidents.impact: Stole passwords, emails, session cookies, and communications from compromised government entities between March and May 2026, consistent with strategic intelligence-collection objectives.

incidents.vector: Exploited a poorly secured technical function in the agency's user management portal (BAP) to gain unauthorized access.
incidents.impact: Potentially exposed personal data (names, addresses, phone numbers, email, national ID numbers) of several hundred individuals and businesses; disrupted EU customs systems including the Import Control System 2.

incidents.victim: Multiple organizations with internet-exposed VPN appliances (US and Europe)
incidents.vector: Compromised SonicWall, Palo Alto Networks, and Fortinet VPN appliances, then deployed the newly identified GhostFrame post-exploitation framework on VMware ESXi hosts to harvest credentials and pivot across virtual machines.
incidents.impact: Enabled double-extortion ransomware deployment tied to the Settra ransomware operation (tracked as TAG-218); at least four victims confirmed published on Settra's leak site between August and October 2026.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the company's drone flight-planning software and planted a malicious update.
incidents.impact: Quantum Systems shut down its IT network; German defense forces grounded drones supplied to the Ukrainian military while the company investigated. The malicious update was not delivered to any drones.

incidents.victim: ActiveCloud and three other Russian/Belarusian cloud hosting providers
incidents.vector: Unspecified ransomware attack against cloud hosting infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Brought down ActiveCloud's web hosting and email services for nearly a week; three other Russian cloud providers were hit by similar unattributed attacks over the past month.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack detected across campus IT systems and applications, forcing a shutdown of university devices and WiFi.
incidents.impact: The BYOD ransomware group claims to have stolen more than 1 million Social Security numbers belonging to students and employees; multiple digital services remained disrupted for days.

incidents.vector: Attackers accessed Expedia's network via a third-party data platform provider.
incidents.impact: Hackers leaked company data after Expedia refused to pay a ransom; the n0n data extortion group claimed responsibility.

incidents.vector: Scammers tricked city staff into changing a contractor's payment details over a five-month social-engineering campaign.
incidents.impact: The city paid $14.7 million to fraudsters before the scheme was discovered when the real contractor reported a missing payment.

incidents.vector: Used an unrevoked cloud access key originally issued to a third-party AI service provider, then deployed the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework to escalate access across the company's internal network and cloud environments.
incidents.impact: Attacker reached across 10 cloud environments over nearly two days searching for cryptocurrency-wallet secrets and credentials; no evidence attacker accessed XDR customer integration credentials, though some customers were told to reissue credentials as a precaution.

incidents.victim: 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes and other IoT devices (global)
incidents.vector: Device manufacturer Videostrong Technology intentionally shipped TV boxes preloaded with malware that enrolled devices in a botnet and resold their internet connections as residential proxies.
incidents.impact: Google and industry partners dismantled the XCPE botnet, severing access to more than 10 million additional compromised devices used for proxy and advertising fraud.

incidents.victim: Hundreds of European supermarkets and some medical facilities
incidents.vector: Gained unauthorized access to internet-exposed Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO refrigeration controllers via weak default credentials and command-injection flaws, setting units to defrost mode.
incidents.impact: Hundreds of supermarkets across France and 10+ other European countries forced to discard spoiled food, with some units reaching 50°C and causing fires; French authorities attributed the attacks to the IRGC's Shahid Kaveh unit.

incidents.vector: Attacker stole an access key Cursor had issued to AI training platform Fireworks.ai, then used leaked customer-communication credentials to upload a malicious version of Anthropic's Claude Code VS Code extension to Cursor's marketplace.
incidents.impact: The malicious extension installed SSH backdoors on roughly 5,000 systems; Uber is separately notifying drivers that their data was stolen following the related Fireworks.ai breach.

incidents.vector: Exploited the PHP2Shell remote-code-execution vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618/109619) alongside a DynamicCLI privilege-escalation flaw to drop a web shell.
incidents.impact: Attacks began in late October, about a week after patches were released; compromised gateways received follow-on proxy and wiper components via the web shell.

incidents.victim: ConnectWise and downstream Microsoft 365 customers (2,250+ tenants)
incidents.vector: Following compromise of ConnectWise application credentials, Storm-0940 used the ARTEX AI framework to accelerate sign-in attempts against more than 2,250 downstream Microsoft 365 tenants.
incidents.impact: Follow-on activity involved abuse of Microsoft Graph, application credential theft, and privilege changes across affected tenants.
